title: Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust--Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation
abstract: arXiv:2610.31971v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly participate in negotiations on behalf of individuals and organizations, yet they remain vulnerable to manipulation, particularly in repeated multi-party interactions. Classical multi-agent systems address this challenge through explicit trust and reputation models, whereas existing work on LLM negotiation largely treats trust as an emergent phenomenon. We investigate whether LLM agents can form useful trust estimates from prior interactions and leverage them to improve future negotiation outcomes. We introduce a repeated, multi-party, multi-issue negotiation framework in which recurring agents participate in a sequence of negotiation games while one participant covertly attempts to prevent agreement. translated_title: 知道该信任谁还不够：重复多方LLM谈判中的信任-协议鸿沟
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体越来越多地代表个人和组织参与谈判，但它们仍然容易受到操纵，尤其是在重复的多方互动中。经典的多智能体系统通过显式的信任与声誉模型来应对这一挑战，而现有的LLM谈判研究大多将信任视为一种涌现现象。我们研究了LLM智能体能否从先前的交互中形成有用的信任估计，并利用它们来改善未来的谈判结果。我们引入了一个重复的、多方的、多议题的谈判框架，其中反复出现的智能体参与一系列谈判博弈，同时一名参与者暗中试图阻止达成协议。每次博弈结束后，智能体会评估其对手，并维护延续至后续谈判的成对信任估计。我们比较了信任感知与信任无关的智能体，并分析了……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本文提出了一个重复多方、多议题的LLM谈判框架，发现LLM智能体虽然能从历史交互中形成有用的信任估计并识别暗中阻挠协议的对手，但知道该信任谁并不足以保证达成协议，从而揭示了“信任-协议鸿沟”。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a repeated multi-party, multi-issue LLM negotiation framework and shows that even when LLM agents form useful trust estimates from prior interactions and can identify a covert agreement-blocker, knowing whom to trust is not enough to secure agreements, revealing a "trust-agreement gap."
